show.title: Lost in Yonkers
show.author: Neil Simon
show.description: Neil Simon’s Pulitzer Prize–winning Lost in Yonkers is a richly funny, deeply human comedy about family, survival, and growing up when you’re least prepared to do so. When two young brothers are sent to live with their formidable grandmother, they’re plunged into a household full of unforgettable characters: a childlike aunt, a sharp-tongued matriarch, and a mysterious uncle with ties to the mob. Simon’s trademark humor crackles throughout, delivering laugh-out-loud moments alongside unexpected tenderness. Widely regarded as Simon’s most accomplished play, Lost in Yonkers balances comedy and compassion, reminding us that even the most complicated families can shape us in surprising—and often hilarious—ways.

show.author: Kevin Murphy and Dan Studney
show.description:
Inspired by the original 1936 film of the same name, this raucous musical comedy takes a tongue-in-cheek look at the hysteria caused when clean-cut kids fall prey to marijuana, leading them on a hysterical downward spiral filled with evil jazz music, sex and violence.

You won’t be able to resist the spoofy fun of Reefer Madness. The addictive, clever musical numbers range from big Broadway-style showstoppers to swing tunes like “Down at the Ol’ Five and Dime” and the Vegas-style “Listen to Jesus, Jimmy,” featuring J.C. Himself leading a chorus of showgirl angels. Refeer Madness is a highly stylized and satirical political commentary that will leave you wanting more.

show.description: This psychological thriller based on Stephen King's novel Misery follows successful romance novelist Paul Sheldon, who is rescued from a car crash and wakes up captive in a secluded home owned by his self-identified "number one fan," Annie Wilkes. While Paul is convalescing, Annie reads the manuscript of his latest book and becomes enraged when she discovers the author has killed off her favorite character, Misery Chastain. Annie forces Paul to write a new Misery novel and he quickly realizes Annie has no intention of letting him go. The irate Annie has Paul writing as if his life depends on it – and it does.

Running alongside the trial is the children's fascination with their mysterious neighbor, Arthur 'Boo' Radley.

show.description: When Wilbur, a small pig with a big heart, learns that his future on the farm is uncertain, he finds an unexpected champion in Charlotte — a wise and wonderful spider with a talent for writing. With the help of Fern, who understands the language of animals, and Templeton, a reluctant but resourceful rat, Charlotte hatches a plan to change Wilbur's fate. Gentle, funny, and deeply moving, Charlotte's Web is a classic, heartwarming tale that celebrates loyalty, kindness, and what it truly means to be a friend.

show.title: Steel Magnolias
show.author: Robert Harling
show.description: Set in Truvy Jones's beauty salon in Chinquapin, Louisiana, the gathering place for the town's women, the play opens as Truvy takes on Annelle Dupuy, a timid newcomer still finding her footing. Regulars include Shelby Eatenton, a young nurse getting ready for her wedding; her mother M'Lynn, a mental health counselor; Clairee Belcher, a sharp, well-off widow; and Ouiser Boudreaux, the town's resident grouch. Through gossip, jokes and heart-to-heart talks across several seasons, the women share happiness and hardship, including the tension caused by Shelby's wish to have children despite the risks of her Type 1 diabetes. The title captures their nature: delicate as magnolias but as tough as steel, in a story that celebrates female friendship while facing love, loss and community.

show.description: In Ivan Menchell's comedy, three Jewish widows get together every month for tea before visiting their husbands' graves, until a widower named Sam upsets the routine and tests their loyalties. Ida is ready for a new beginning, Lucille wants fun and attention, and Doris holds tight to tradition. As Sam's interest in Ida shakes up the group, each woman has to face what it means to love, to let go, and to live fully again, in a story that mixes humor and tenderness while dealing with grief, friendship and the fear of moving on.

show.description: Set in an age of artificial intelligence, Jordan Harrison's play centers on Marjorie, an 85-year-old woman whose memories have become scattered and are slipping away, and the handsome new companion she has been given: a "Prime" programmed to tell the story of her own life back to her. The play asks what we would choose to hold onto, and what we would let go of, if the choice were ours, and through spare, quietly wondrous storytelling it probes the nature of human identity and whether there is anything technology cannot stand in for. Directed by Tim Hass, this four-person, 80-minute play is performed at Dare Arts in Manteo.

Naturally, everything that can go wrong does, helped along by their daughter's hopelessly clueless fiancé and by mounting confusion over which play is actually being performed, thanks to Charlotte's deaf, elderly stage-manager mother, who despises George. show.title: My Fair Lady
show.author: Alan Jay Lerner
show.description: Lerner and Loewe's classic musical, adapted from George Bernard Shaw's play Pygmalion, is a story of transformation that also takes on patronage, class and gender politics. Professor Henry Higgins, a celebrated phonetics expert and determined bachelor, bets his colleague Colonel Pickering that within six months he can teach Eliza Doolittle, a Cockney flower seller, to speak so properly that she can pass as a duchess at an embassy ball. After grueling lessons day and night, Eliza masters 'proper' English and becomes a lady admired across every class; along the way young Freddy Eynsford-Hill falls for her, and she even convinces a self-styled language expert that she is royalty. Through the process Eliza grows close to Pickering and especially to Higgins, yet she is left stranded, now too refined for her old life but with neither the means nor the wish to live as an idle lady on her own. When Higgins refuses to credit her for her own transformation, she walks out, and only then does he realize how much he cares for her. The show closes with Eliza returning to Higgins' home on a deliberately open-ended note, and it is cherished as one of the wittiest and most romantic musicals ever written, with songs such as "Wouldn't It Be Loverly" and "I Could Have Danced All Night."

show.title: The Neverland Project
show.author: Stephen Gregg
show.description: You may think you know the story of Peter Pan, the boy who can fly, along with Neverland, the pirates, the Lost Boys and Tinker Bell, but the man who wrote it all down wasn't actually there. Wendy Moira Angela Darling was, and she sets out to set the record straight by staging a play of her own called The Neverland Project.
